title: ScienceLabValidationReceipt/v1
description: A receipt proving an independent validator checked the scientific output of an engine run, carrying the honest scientific and formal check outcomes. The receipt binds a validator_id to an engine_receipt_id (the engine run whose output was checked) and records the scientific_check (checked / contradicted / inconclusive) and the formal_check (unchecked / checked / proven). CRITICAL INVARIANT (schema + python): formal_check=proven REQUIRES a non-null formal_certificate_ref — a verified, independently-checkable certificate. A SMT-style SAT/UNSAT answer yields at most formal_check=checked (a solver result without a verified certificate is not proven); proven without a certificate is a dishonest upgrade and is rejected. The validation receipt also carries the statistical_support and causal_identification axes (re-asserted here by the validator, independently of the formal axes — formal proof never updates statistical or causal support). The receipt carries the two safety consts (canonical_writes=0, grants_authority=false). Canonical JSON contract: sorted keys, compact separators, UTF-8, no NaN/Infinity, trailing newline.

allOf.$comment: formal_check=proven REQUIRES a non-null formal_certificate_ref. A verified certificate is the load-bearing artifact for a proven formal statement: without it, the statement is at most checked (a solver result). Encoding the SAT/UNSAT-is-not-proven rule at the schema layer; re-enforced in python (proven_requires_certificate).

receipt_id.description: Content-addressed identity: sha256 over the canonical encoding of the receipt (without this field), prefixed 'sha256:'. Computed by the python receipt builder.

engine_receipt_id.description: The receipt_id of the ScienceLabEngineReceipt/v1 whose output this validation checked. The validation receipt binds back to the engine run so the compute lineage and the validation lineage tie together.

validator_id.description: The logical identifier of the independent validator that produced the check. Names which validator discharged the scientific/formal check.

scientific_check.description: The outcome of checking the engine output against the claim: checked (the output is consistent with the claim), contradicted (the output contradicts the claim), inconclusive (the check could not reach a verdict). NOT a formal verdict — it is the scientific consistency of the computed output.

formal_check.description: The level of formal verification the validator discharged: unchecked (no formal statement checked), checked (a solver returned SAT/UNSAT or a checked-but-unverified result), proven (a verified, independently-checkable certificate exists — REQUIRES a non-null formal_certificate_ref). A SMT-style answer without a verified certificate yields at most checked; proven without a certificate is rejected.

formal_certificate_ref.description: An ArtifactRef/v1 pointing at the verified, independently-checkable formal certificate, or null when no certificate exists (formal_check != proven). REQUIRED non-null when formal_check=proven (encoded by the allOf/if-then above). Carried inline as a structural object when present (schema_version const ArtifactRef/v1, media_type, digest, size_bytes, optional path); the full field contract is enforced at the python layer.

media_type.description: IANA-style media type of the referenced certificate payload (e.g. application/vnd.srlab.formal-certificate+json).

digest.description: Content digest of the certificate bytes: sha256 + 64 lowercase hex digits.

size_bytes.description: Non-negative integer byte count of the referenced certificate payload.

path.description: Optional portable repo-relative path to the certificate bytes. Validated for portability at the python layer; the digest remains authoritative.

statistical_support.description: The statistical support axis as re-asserted by the validator (not_applicable / none / weak / moderate / strong). INDEPENDENT of formal_check: a formal proof never updates statistical support. The validator asserts this from its own statistical evidence, not from the formal certificate.

causal_identification.description: The causal identification axis as re-asserted by the validator (not_applicable / assumed / partially_identified / identified). INDEPENDENT of formal_check: a formal proof never updates causal identification.

created_utc.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp at seconds precision (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). No offset, no fractional seconds.

canonical_writes.description: Safety const: a receipt is immutable once authored. Always 0; a non-zero value is a contract violation.

grants_authority.description: Safety const: a receipt never grants authority on its own. Always false; a true value is a contract violation. A proven formal statement is still an admission of formal verification, not an authorization.
